POLITICAL COMMENT & SATIRE

CONSERVATIVE
RESTORE BRITAIN

By Steve English · 17 October 2026

Reform gets lectured about accepting people who left the Conservatives. So let’s look at the Conservative connections surrounding Rupert Lowe.

1. Susan Hall: a senior Tory on Restore’s board

Susan Hall, then leader of the Conservative group in the London Assembly, joined the advisory board of Lowe’s original Restore Britain movement.

2. Gavin Williamson: a serving Tory MP

Serving Conservative MP and former Cabinet minister Sir Gavin Williamson also joined Restore’s advisory board while it operated as a political movement.

3. The Sunak family business connection

Lowe and Rishi Sunak’s wife, Akshata Murty, were fellow directors of Digme Fitness Limited. Companies House records both appointments on 24 March 2017.

4. A committee place from the Conservatives

In October 2025, the Conservatives gave Lowe one of their allocated places on the Public Accounts Committee. Parliament records his membership from 21 October 2025.

Hall and Williamson stepped away as Restore became a political party in February 2026. That matters, and belongs in the account. It also doesn’t erase the senior Tory backing the original movement received.

My view? Lowe is a very useful political tool for the Conservatives: a rival who can divide Reform’s support. The backstage cartoon is my way of making that political argument.

Yet Reform gets attacked for accepting people who left the Conservatives. If Tory connections are the objection, the same scrutiny should apply to Lowe.

Apparently Tory connections only matter when they’re somebody else’s.
